title: Pointwise causal estimation with weak dose support and Gaussian measurement error
tldr: Under fixed smoothness and polynomially vanishing dose support, the paper establishes matching optimal orders for estimating the causal mean at a prespecified latent dose and for the length of honest confidence intervals with known Gaussian measurement error. It characterizes how these orders change with the error scale and constructs an observable estimator with an interval that guarantees finite-sample coverage throughout the model class.
abstract: Under calibrated public density envelopes satisfying \(c_{\mathrm{lo}}\le(\kappa+1)2^\kappa\le c_{\mathrm{hi}}\), where \(c_{\mathrm{lo}}\) and \(c_{\mathrm{hi}}\) are the density-envelope constants and \(\kappa\) is the design-decay exponent, we characterize optimal estimation and honest interval length for the population causal mean at a prespecified latent dose when treatment is measured with Gaussian error and local dose support may vanish polynomially. The model has two observed strata, compact latent-dose support, bounded potential outcomes, schedule-level conditional exchangeability, and classical measurement error with known standard deviation \(\sigma\in[0,1/4]\). Conditional mean functions have Hölder exponent \(\beta\in(0,1]\), and conditional dose densities satisfy these public polynomial envelopes with \(\kappa\in[0,2]\). For this calibrated class and any fixed noncoverage probability \(\alpha\in(0,1/2)\), minimax expected absolute error and minimum worst-law expected length of honest connected \((1-\alpha)\)-coverage intervals have matching orders, uniformly over the error scale. For sample size \(n\), the characterization combines a direct weak-design regime with rate \(n^{-\beta/(2\beta+\kappa+1)}\), an intermediate Gaussian-inversion regime, and a compact-support regime. Neighboring rate formulas are comparable throughout fixed multiplicative neighborhoods of both transition thresholds. Every fixed error scale \(\sigma\in(0,1/4]\) yields order \((\log\log n/\log n)^\beta\) for this calibrated class. An observable estimator selects among Fourier, polynomial, and constant inverse weights using public error certificates, with the declared small-sample fallback; its associated interval has finite-sample coverage \(1-\alpha\) for every \(\alpha\in(0,1)\). Under the same envelope calibration, matching lower bounds follow from bounded Bernoulli structural alternatives whose causal means are separated while their complete observed samples remain difficult to distinguish.
score_rationale: The verified uniform frontier is a substantial theoretical contribution, while publication requires a more focused exposition, numerical assessment of the explicit procedure, and sharper attribution of methodological antecedents.
